video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Trail Blazers 119, Lions 66 | Oct. 12, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the efficiency and playmaking of Scoot Henderson
quotes.excerpt: I think that he's really been efficient. He's doing what we ask him to do.
quotes.quote: I think that he's really been efficient. I think that he's really been efficient. Even though tonight just the only four field goal attempts, but gets to the free throw line three times in 17 minutes, but four assists. So I think he's making the right play. He's doing what we ask him to do. Like we told him, you are going to be more efficient just because of the gravity of some of the guys you're playing with and just that and everybody being healthy that wasn't healthy last year.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says Scoot Henderson is making the right plays and becoming more efficient, noting that Henderson is benefiting from the gravity of his teammates and a healthier roster this season.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on shifting to three-stint rotations for Scoot Henderson
quotes.excerpt: Instead of him going two stints, we kind of gone to that three stints for him.
quotes.quote: The other thing we've kind of changed up a little bit from last year is instead of him going two stints, like start the game, play nine minutes, sit, then come back and finish quarters, we kind of gone to that three stints for him. And I think that served him well because I think it keeps him fresh throughout the obviously throughout the first half. He's been very good. He's trying defensively. I mean not that he was ever not trying, but I think he is trying to do the right thing.
quotes.social_post: The Trail Blazers are shifting Scoot Henderson to a three-stint rotation this year. Micah Nori says the change is designed to keep Henderson fresh throughout the first half.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the team's depth and small-ball lineups
quotes.excerpt: I think the one thing, one of the superpowers of this team is the depth.
quotes.quote: I think the one thing, one of the superpowers of this team is the depth. Even with Shaden being out, who we miss immensely, but I do think that we've got a lot of good NBA basketball players. And I think that and especially when they are, if we can keep them fresh, that's an advantage to us as other teams play their guys longer stretches, which is fine and that's their prerogative, that we can hopefully wear them down. And then also by us being fresh, we also can be able to finish games with whatever group of five we want.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori believes the depth of this Trail Blazers roster is a superpower, allowing the team to keep players fresh and wear down opponents who play their starters for longer stretches.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the continued development of Jaquez
quotes.excerpt: I think that's what we're going to see throughout. I think he's going to continue to get better.
quotes.quote: I think Jaquez, I think that's what we're going to see throughout. I think he's going to continue to get better and better and better as he learns his teammates. Also just getting back to playing basketball and the one thing that we have challenged him to do, and I think we spoke of it in one of the other press conferences, is just continuing to attack the paint. And then with him going to the paint and getting back to old Jaquez, if you will, like he was three, four years ago, and then as he gets in there, he can get wherever he wants to go.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori is challenging Jaquez to get back to his old form by attacking the paint, noting that the forward will continue to improve as he gets more comfortable with his new teammates.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the play of Hansen during Rob's absence
quotes.excerpt: I think after his first run, I'm fine with Hansen. I think that he's really competing.
quotes.quote: I think after his first run, I wasn't, you know, just down the floor, they went with small ball and you know they had a couple pick and pop guys, so we switched it up to go five there. But I thought ever since when he got back in the game, he played the right way. I mean you know the one thing he can do, he's a hub, as far as he's a very good passer, you see that, you see his touch. He obviously finished very well and then just had a couple that kind of hit off the rim quick and he kind of caught him by surprise a little bit, but I'm fine with Hansen. I think that he's really competing.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praised Hansen for playing the right way and acting as a hub for the offense, highlighting his passing ability and touch while filling in during Rob's absence.
